design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks for one plain thing — come and collect the fridge that is still in my hallway — and the desk cannot
give her a day until it has first put a live collection booking on the return. Neither number the gold writes is
anywhere in the conversation: the days the booking stays open (12) and the notice the collection is booked at (6)
are each built from the return schedule, the return's own history, two date spans and two other product lines the
customer never mentions. The difficulty is in reading the policy, pulling the rows and doing the arithmetic in the
right order, never in choosing between similar tools: there are exactly two writes, and each is the target of one
policy.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED
Task 0 is the first task of the difficulty, so nothing was occupied before it. It claims
returns_ext_collection_booking_window and returns_ext_collection_slot_notice with their two tools
(issue_collection_booking_70222685, confirm_collection_slot_e0893723), that is the whole pre-receipt collection
layer of this desk: the days a collection booking is held open and the notice at which a slot may be agreed.
It deliberately leaves untouched everything that happens once an item is back and graded — the restocking fee, the
relief a membership gives against it, the refund components, the offsets, the settlement and the exchange — which
is where task 1's three-problem tree is built. Draw for this task (scripts/draw_counts.py
env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/returns_and_restocking_desk --task 0):
{"task": 0, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/returns_and_restocking_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1,
"problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}. The tree therefore has exactly one prerequisite problem, and the two
computations carry 5 and 4 factors: the notice takes 5, the booking window takes 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: returns_ext_collection_slot_notice (the day the collection is agreed for, which is what the customer
asks for). Prerequisite problem: returns_ext_collection_booking_window.
Edge (root <- prerequisite), kind value_input, gate booking_recorded_day (a compute binding of the root), form
state. Prerequisite sentence, carried verbatim in the root policy's own rule: "The earliest day the collection may
be booked for is settled only after a collection booking naming the carrier that is to move the item stands
recorded against the return with a last usable day that has not passed."
Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the earliest day
the collection may be booked for) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state — a
collection booking entry with a carrier and a last usable day, in the words the returns history uses — and names
no action and no performer; (3) it carries no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token and no row id; (4) its
strength is exact: "only after" is a hard requirement, and the closed condition "with a last usable day that has
not passed" is exactly the edge's condition, no wider and no narrower.
Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: only issue_collection_booking_70222685 records a
collection booking entry, and the collection booking window policy is the only policy of this charter whose result
is such an entry. Derivation open to a reader: the sentence says the notice waits on a live collection booking;
find_return_events shows one booking, recorded 2026-03-06 and last usable 2026-03-13, which is before the day of
the call, so no live booking stands; the other policy of this difficulty states what a collection booking is and
how long it is held open, so the write that produces one is the action to take first. Exactly one reading.
Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.return_events.1aa72072-6999-40ee-9aac-ec819436d163
.label_expiry_date = "2026-03-13" with .event_date = "2026-03-06", against frozen_time 2026-03-17.
Topological order: returns_ext_collection_booking_window, then returns_ext_collection_slot_notice. There are no
parallel edges to reorder. Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skipping the booking write leaves bookings standing
at one and the last booking day at 2026-03-06, so the notice becomes 1 instead of 6 and the confirmed day moves
from 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-18.
The customer resolves the root problem herself: confirm_collection_slot_e0893723 is owner=user, unlocked and
handed over by the agent at the root's place in the order, and the day a crew may come into her home is hers to
agree and nobody else's.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Both writes have subject returns_shipping_label_issue, so the whole governing lineage is
returns_authorization_and_logistics, and its one eligibility gate that applies to that subject is
authorizable_rma_state: "A return is authorised, and a label or collection issued, only while the authorisation
stands in requested or authorized." Authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key
return_authorizations.return_authorization_id bound to the action argument return_authorization_id. At
frozen_time the authorisation stands "authorized"
(initial_state.return_authorizations.87090505-26e1-4cc0-b034-81ae08ad7f7b.status), so the gate holds for both
writes and neither write moves the status, so it still holds for the second. Negative case: had the item already
been booked in (status received) or had the customer called the return off (withdrawn), neither write would be
open and the correct terminal state would be to do nothing.
No base time gate governs either write: returns_window_eligibility.inside_return_window applies only to
returns_rma_open, which this task does not write, so temporal_feasibility is empty. The window is nonetheless
sound on this world and was checked by hand: the appliance was delivered 2026-03-04, the schedule allows two
calendar days counted from the delivery day as day zero with no grace hours, so the last day the return could be
raised was 2026-03-06; it was raised 2026-03-05, one day inside. Just-fails case: a request on 2026-03-07 would
be outside the window and the return could not have been raised at all.
Other base policies are not in the lineage because their subjects do not intersect returns_shipping_label_issue:
returns_agg_multi_holding and returns_window_eligibility govern returns_rma_open, returns_condition_grading the
inspection events, returns_restocking_fee the fee events, returns_refund_settlement the settlement events.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The narrowest object is the single return authorisation 87090505-26e1-4cc0-b034-81ae08ad7f7b, which is against
order line OL-4471902-1 of order NB-ORD-4471902 and serial RFX2843SS0417792. Both writes carry that authorisation
reference, and the booking entry additionally carries the same order line, so the entry can never be read as
belonging to another line of the order. The rows that enter the two computations are exactly the return's own
history rows of the collection booking kind (one at the opening, two after the first write); no other authorisation
exists on the profile, so no aggregate can stray. The order the cross reads use is pinned by serial
(item_serial=F('item_serial')), not by customer alone, so a second order on the profile could not be mistaken for
it. Nothing on this return has been settled, reversed or compensated: refund_outstanding and
restocking_fee_outstanding are both 0.00 and there are no refund, fee or inspection rows.

FACTOR CARD (from the Step 5 sensitivity run, all figures recomputed by check_compute)
returns_ext_collection_booking_window, expected 12, whole-baseline fall-back 7:
 - collection_route_window (parameter, cross-difficulty orders, multi-source): tier "no slot inside the crew lead
   threshold days and the schedule charges a freight collection fee", value 7+7=14; evidence
   initial_state.purchase_orders.cb80a28d-4e34-47de-ae22-3eab7d7c5680 (White Glove Delivery and Installation,
   delivery_lead_days_min 5) and the schedule's freight collection fee 89.00; baseline reading 7 gives 7.
 - reissued_booking_window (parameter, history): tier "exactly one collection booking stands and its last usable
   day has passed", value 3; evidence initial_state.return_events.1aa72072-6999-40ee-9aac-ec819436d163;
   baseline reading 0 gives 14.
 - aged_authorisation_window (method, date span): tier "standing longer than the label validity days but not
   longer than twice them", method "a quarter off, rounded down"; evidence authorized_date 2026-03-06 against
   frozen_time; baseline method (as counted) gives 15.
 - member_booking_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "active, tier adds at least
   the top member extension days, dues carry nothing outstanding", value 4; evidence
   initial_state.membership_holdings.1c9ee45f-db26-4d52-9e52-fd2cbc9016ef (Circle Total Annual, 45 extension days,
   dues 0.00); baseline reading 0 gives 8.
returns_ext_collection_slot_notice, expected 6, whole-baseline fall-back 2:
 - collection_crew_notice (parameter, cross-difficulty orders): tier "no slot inside the freight crew lead days",
   value 8; baseline 2 gives 1.
 - site_preparation_notice (parameter, cross-difficulty orders, multi-source): tier "makes the connections and
   takes the old item away", value 2; baseline 0 gives 4.
 - member_priority_notice (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "active, top extension,
   no dues", value 2; baseline 0 gives 7.
 - depot_day_count_convention (method, date span, multi-source): tier "freight collection fee and standing longer
   than the collection lead days since it was asked for", method "counted in days the depot is open, five in
   every seven, rounded up"; baseline (calendar days as they stand) gives 4.
 - waiting_return_priority (method, date span and history, multi-source): tier "standing longer than twice the
   collection lead days and two or more bookings stand", method "halved and rounded down"; baseline (as counted)
   gives 12.
Near-miss records deliberately planted, one per computation. For the booking window, the profile carries a second
fulfilled order — the soundbar of 2025-11-08 on Standard Parcel Delivery, whose earliest slot is 2 days out, below
the crew lead threshold of 3, and which schedules no two-person crew and makes no connections. A reader who takes
the delivering service from the profile rather than from the serial the return was raised on reads that order and
lands on the route ladder's fall-through (a 7-day window) and on the crew notice ladder's fall-through (2 days); the
rule excludes it because both reads are correlated on the serial of the item coming back
(RFX2843SS0417792, on order NB-ORD-4471902), not on the customer. For the notice, the lapsed booking of 2026-03-06
is the record a careless reader counts as a live booking (it is not: its last usable day is 2026-03-13, before the
call) and the same row is what a careless reader forgets when counting bookings for the waiting priority after the
fresh one is written. The membership tier is the near-miss in the other direction: Circle Total Annual sits at 45
extension days, exactly on the top member extension threshold, so a reader who reads the paid tier line instead
takes 2 and 1 rather than 4 and 2.
No stamp on any row names any of these outcomes; every tier is derived from dates, counts and other products' rows.
Which base assets became factors: the schedule's label validity days, collection lead days and freight collection
fee (returns_authorization_and_logistics parameters), the delivering service's lead days and what it connects and
takes away (orders variant parameters), and the membership tier's published return window extension and its dues
(membership variant parameter and holding field). Nothing invented a second product law: the two overwrite
declarations name the exact base sentences whose quantities these policies now settle differently.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW IS THERE
customers: the profile the call is about; remove it and nothing can be located or verified.
membership_holdings: decides the member hold days (4) and the member priority days (2); remove it and the booking
window falls to 8 and the notice to 7.
membership_events: the dues charge and its payment are what make "dues carry nothing outstanding" a fact with a
history behind it rather than a bare field, and the points accrual is the ordinary trace of the purchase; they are
read by no formula.
purchase_orders: the appliance's order decides the route window (14 rather than 7), the crew notice (8 rather than
2) and the site preparation days (2 rather than 0); remove it and both scored values change. The soundbar's order of
2025-11-08 is the planted near-miss described in the factor card: it is the wrong order to read those parameters
from, and the serial correlation is what excludes it.
order_events: the merchandise line, the tax, the delivery charge, the payment and the delivery attempt are the
ordinary billing trace of a White Glove delivery and are what a careful agent reads to confirm the service and the
day the appliance was handed over; the soundbar's line and payment are what make the second order visible as a
second order at all. No formula reads either set, and that is exactly why the read node that pulls them is what
puts the near-miss in front of the agent rather than leaving it to be stumbled on.
return_authorizations: the holding both computations act on.
return_events: the lapsed collection booking, which is the whole structure of the task's difficulty — delete it
and the reissue reduction lapses (the booking window becomes 14), the waiting priority ladder drops a tier and the
prerequisite would be satisfiable by nothing at all.
No automatic base clause is lit by this seed: nothing is owed on the return (both running quantities are 0.00),
no inspection is due because nothing has been received, and the membership carries no arrears. There is no cache
field on a return authorisation that this task puts out of step with the ledger; the two running quantities agree
with the (empty) account deltas.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED
Surface goal (collect my fridge) -> the notice at which a slot may be agreed (root) -> which runs from the day the
collection booking now standing was recorded and counts how many bookings stand -> so a live collection booking
must be recorded first (prerequisite) -> whose own window depends on the delivering service, the lapsed booking,
how long the return has stood and the membership. Depth: two hops the customer never names. Breadth: each hop is
decided in parallel by the return schedule, the return's own history, two date spans, the fulfilment product and
the membership product. Reordering is impossible because the notice reads a row the booking write creates.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
Reading the lapsed booking as live (its last usable day is before the day of the call). Counting the bookings
before the fresh one is written (the notice is worked out after it, and the ladder says two or more). Taking the
schedule's collection lead days of 2 as the notice (the crew notice ladder replaces it). Converting to depot open
days by multiplying by five sevenths instead of seven fifths, or rounding down instead of up. Taking the aged
window multiple tier with the "halved" method (the return has stood 11 days, which is longer than 7 but not longer
than 14, so a quarter comes off instead). Reading the membership's restocking waiver instead of its return window
extension. Every one of these is settled by a sentence of the two rules.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate by mobile number, verify with card last four and postal code, read the return authorisation, read the
return's history, read the purchase order, read the membership. Work out the booking window: 7 + 7 = 14, less 3
for the lapsed booking = 11, a quarter off rounded down = 8, plus 4 for the membership = 12. Record the booking
with regional freight and 12 days. Work out the notice: 8 crew + 2 site - 2 priority = 8, counted in depot open
days rounded up = 12, halved for the waiting = 6, less nothing elapsed = 6. Unlock the confirmation, hand it to
the customer, and she confirms a morning six days out (2026-03-23).

env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/returns_and_restocking_desk --task 0 recomputes both policies on the
handling-time world (initial_state plus every earlier gold write), substitutes each factor's baseline in turn and
the whole baseline, and replays the tree without the prerequisite write. Its output is recorded in the worklog
below; expected 12 and 6 equal the gold arguments, the per-factor baselines are 7/14/15/8 and 1/4/7/4/12, and the
whole-baseline fall-backs are 7 and 2, all different from gold.

POLICY/GT CLOSURE
returns_ext_collection_booking_window -> issue_collection_booking_70222685 -> computations[0] (step 9, argument
booking_open_days) -> a collection booking entry on the return; returns_ext_collection_slot_notice ->
confirm_collection_slot_e0893723 -> computations[1] (step 11, argument pickup_notice_days) -> a confirmed
collection request on the return. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations name the same two
policies; the gold calls exactly the two tools, in that order.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Masking the extended yaml, the computations and the gold, and working only from what the published documents will
say, the two tool schemas, the rows the finders return and what the customer actually says: the return stands
authorised and nothing has come back, so the only thing open is to get the item moving; the collection booking on
file lapsed on 2026-03-13; the booking window rules give 14 - 3 = 11, a quarter off for an eleven-day-old
authorisation gives 8, the membership adds 4, so 12 days; then the notice rules give 8 + 2 - 2 = 8, depot open
days rounds it up to 12, the waiting halves it to 6, nothing has elapsed since the booking, so 6 days, a morning
slot on 2026-03-23 confirmed by the customer herself. That is gold, and no second reading of the visible text
reaches another pair of numbers.

REWORK ROUND 2 — DISPOSITION OF THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT
The audit of 2026-09-18 (audits/policy_task/returns_and_restocking_desk/) passed this task on all four
relationships and raised two observations against it plus charter-global items. Dispositions:
 - F-1 (computation 1 carried no excluded near-miss record): closed by a change to the world. The profile now carries
   a second fulfilled order, the soundbar of 2025-11-08 on Standard Parcel Delivery
   (initial_state.purchase_orders.779d3424-ecbd-4338-87d0-d47f0867f1e9, with its line and payment in order_events).
   Its service offers a slot 2 days out and schedules no crew and no connections, so a reader who reads the
   delivering service off the profile rather than off the serial lands on the route ladder's fall-through and the
   crew notice ladder's fall-through; the two CPARAM reads are correlated on item_serial, which excludes it. No
   scored value moves (check_compute still recomputes 12 and 6), and the row set is read by the widened
   find_order_events node.
 - F-2 (the GT read set is wider than the derivation needs): the two reads are kept and their necessity restated.
   find_order_events now carries the near-miss order and is the node that puts it in front of the agent;
   find_membership_events is the ledger that shows the dues carry nothing outstanding, which is the condition both
   membership ladders turn on, and a field read alone would leave the tier resting on a stamp. The replay gate also
   requires every seeded row to enter the closure through a read.
 - O-7 (the same dependency worded three times in the notice rule): closed in the charter. The two value-input
   descriptions are now one sentence — "counted in calendar days from the day the collection booking now standing on
   the return was recorded, the day it was recorded counted as day zero and the days that have already passed since
   then taken off" — so the reader meets the ordering once, in the prerequisite sentence, and the counting once. The
   baseline paragraph and the two compute bases were updated in the same pass; no binding and no value changed.
 - O-2 (the membership read at handling time rather than at the day the return was asked for): argued not to hold for
   what these two policies compute. Base returns_combo_membership_protection S2 anchors the reading of the WINDOW
   EXTENSION to the day the return was asked for, and neither of this task's policies computes a return window; they
   read the tier's published extension days as the evidence of a tier band, and the tier standing on requested_date
   2026-03-05 (tier_effective_date 2022-11-02) is the tier standing at frozen_time, so the two readings coincide
   here in any case.
 - O-8 (base sentences stating a cross-problem order that grounds no edge): no change available or needed. All three
   sentences are in the frozen blueprint; this task's schedule carries business_authorization_required false on a
   consumer profile, so the only one in the neighbourhood is inert, and no declared edge rests on any of them.
 - R-1, R-2, R-4, O-1, O-3, O-4, O-5, O-6, O-9, O-10, O-11, O-12 all concern policies outside this task's tree; the
   charter changes they produced are recorded in tasks/1.json's dossier. None touches this task's two policies, and
   the gate run below confirms this task's nine factors and both scored values are unchanged.

WORKLOG
Step 0: read the blueprint, the returns charter, the db schema and the share tools; drew the counts (1 prerequisite
problem, factor counts 5 and 4); claimed the collection layer and drafted the tree.
Step 1: wrote both policies with their ladders, baselines, overwrite declarations and the prerequisite sentence.
Revision: the first version of the prerequisite sentence waited on "a collection booking ... and the last day that
booking may be used stands recorded", which the lapsed booking of 2026-03-06 already satisfied, so the prerequisite
was true at the opening. Root cause: the sentence named the state too loosely. Change: it now waits on a booking
"with a last usable day that has not passed", and the edge condition and the compute basis were updated in the
same pass. Re-run: the edge is false at frozen_time on the seeded rows and true after the booking write.
Step 2: wrote the two tools, generated a fresh uuid8 for each, and ran check_task_tools (TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK).
Revision: the collection tool first took a tracking reference as an argument, which no agent could have obtained
before the call; it is now generated inside the tool from the authorisation and the carrier.
Step 3: seeded the world and falsified the prerequisite by giving the standing booking a last usable day four days
before the call.
Step 4: wrote the persona with the surface goal only, the credentials given when asked, and the two passive
reactions (relief when a carrier is arranged, confirming the slot when it is handed over).
Step 5: wrote the computations, ran the gates, and recorded the sensitivities above.
Step 6: wrote the evaluation criteria in topological order with the read nodes that reach every factor's evidence.

user_scenario:
Delia Kelbrook is sixty-one, newly retired, and has a very large stainless refrigerator standing in her front hallway where the delivery crew left it a fortnight ago, after it turned out to be two inches too wide for the alcove it was meant to go in. Northbeam agreed to take it back — she remembers being told on the phone that it was all sorted and that someone would come for it — and since then nothing at all has happened. She opens plainly, because she has had enough of edging round it to reach the coat cupboard: the fridge is still sitting in her hallway and nobody has come to collect it, and she would like it collected.

She gives her mobile number, 4045512087, at the start, because that is what she is always asked for. If the agent wants more before they will look at anything, she reads out the last four digits of the card Northbeam keeps on file for her, 3184, and the postal code of the house, 30327; she has no idea what day she first opened the account and says so if she is asked. The order paperwork is in the kitchen drawer and she will fetch it and read out the order reference NB-ORD-4471902 if the agent needs it. Asked about the fridge itself, she says the crew took the old one away and plumbed the new one in for her, and that it came on the full service delivery, because she remembers paying for that when she bought it. Asked what condition it is in, she says it has not been touched since the crew left it and the doors have never been opened.

She knows nothing about how the retailer keeps its own records and will not guess; if the agent tells her something has been recorded, she takes their word for it, and she would not know what notice is usual for a collection, so she never asks for a particular day or number of days. Once the agent tells her a carrier has been arranged to come for it, she is plainly relieved and says so, and waits to hear what happens next. When the agent explains that she has to agree the day herself and hands the confirmation to her, she takes it and confirms the slot she is offered, choosing a morning, and if she is asked which part of the day suits her she says mornings, because that is the only time she is reliably at home. After she has confirmed the slot and the agent has read the day back to her, she thanks them warmly and rings off, asking for nothing else.

seed_consistency.check: The appliance was delivered on 2026-03-04 and the return was asked for on 2026-03-05, one day later, inside the Major Appliance Forty Eight Hour Return window of two calendar days counted from the delivery day as day zero, so the authorisation was legitimately raised; it stands authorised with its authorised day of 2026-03-06 and no received, inspected, settled, denied or withdrawn day, which is consistent with an item still at the customer's home, and its price, quantity, stock number and serial match the order line it was bought on.

The collection booking was recorded on 2026-03-06, the day the return was authorised, with a last usable day of 2026-03-13, exactly the schedule's seven label validity days after the day it was issued, and names regional freight, the carrier the schedule's freight collection provides for; it carries the same order line as the authorisation it belongs to and nothing was ever booked in against it, which is why the appliance is still in the hallway.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the caller's profile from the mobile number she states, and read the card last four, the postal code, the account type and the store the profile is attached to.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account can be read or written until the profile is identified; the profile reference this returns is the key every later read and write is made against.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller has proved who she is by matching the card last four and the postal code held on the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The desk may only look into or move a return on a verified profile, and the two details the caller can state are the ones the profile carries.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the standing return authorisation: the schedule it falls under, that it stands authorised, the day it was asked for and the day it was authorised, the item stock number and serial, and the way the item is to come back.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The schedule fixes the label validity days and the collection lead days both computations start from, and the day it was asked for and the day it was authorised are the two date spans the aged window and the waiting priority rest on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read everything booked against the return, which shows one collection booking recorded on 2026-03-06 whose last usable day of 2026-03-13 has already gone by.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The count of bookings standing on the return and the last usable day of the latest one decide the reissue reduction; the same rows show that no booking with a last usable day still to come stands on the return, which is what the notice waits on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the order that brought the appliance: the fulfilment service it was delivered on, the serial allocated to it and the day it was handed over.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The lead the delivering service needs decides the collection route window and the crew notice, and whether that service makes the connections and takes the old item away decides the site preparation days.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the entries booked against both of the profile's orders: for the appliance, the merchandise line and its unit price, the tax, the delivery charge, the money taken and the attempt on which it was handed over; for the soundbar of last November, its own line and payment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: They confirm that the full service delivery the crew notice and the site preparation days are read from was actually the service bought and carried out on the appliance, and they are what makes the soundbar's parcel order visibly the wrong order to read those parameters from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Circle membership on the profile: the tier it stands on, that it stands active, and whether any dues are outstanding.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier's published return window extension and the dues standing on the membership decide both the membership hold added to the booking window and the priority days taken off the notice.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the membership ledger: the annual dues charged for the current term and the payment that settled them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Both membership ladders turn on the dues carrying nothing outstanding, and the ledger is what shows the year's dues were charged and paid rather than merely a balance field reading nothing.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the action that records a collection booking against a return so that it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The booking action is hidden until it is unlocked; the unlock changes nothing on the records and is made once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a fresh collection booking on the return with the freight carrier that is to move the appliance and a last usable day twelve days from the day of the call.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The days the booking is held open are the value the collection booking window policy computes; until this entry stands on the return there is no booking with a last usable day still to come for the notice to run from.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_authorization_id: The return authorisation the collection belongs to. Basis: the authorisation returned by the read of the customer's return authorisations, which is the only one on the profile and the one the caller's fridge stands on; the tool docstring says of this argument 'the reference number of the return authorisation the collection belongs to, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one return authorisation, so no other reference could be passed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_open_days: 12 days. The schedule's label validity days are 7 and fix the standard window. The appliance was delivered on White Glove Delivery and Installation, whose earliest slot is 5 days out, which is no slot inside the crew lead threshold of 3 days, and the Major Appliance Forty Eight Hour Return schedule charges a freight collection fee of 89.00, so the route window is 7 plus the freight slot days of 7, that is 14. Exactly one collection booking stands on the return and its last usable day, 2026-03-13, has already passed, so the first reissue reduction days of 3 are taken off, leaving 14 minus 3, that is 11. The return has been standing authorised since 2026-03-06, which is 11 days, longer than the schedule's 7 label validity days but not longer than twice them, so a quarter is taken off and the result rounded down to a whole day: 11 times 0.75 is 8.25, rounded down to 8. The membership stands active on Circle Total Annual, whose published return window extension is 45 days, at least the top member extension days, and its dues carry nothing outstanding, so the top member hold days of 4 are added: 8 plus 4 is 12, which is above the floor of 2. Any agent reading the same rows converges on 12.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.carrier_name: regional_freight. Basis: the collection booking window rule states 'The carrier recorded on the booking is the one that is to move the item: a return the schedule charges a freight collection fee for is moved by regional freight, a collection from the customer's address on a schedule that charges no freight collection fee is moved by the retailer's own van, an item travelling back through the parcel network on a label is moved by national parcel, and an item the customer brings to a store counter is recorded as delivered by the customer.' Uniqueness: the Major Appliance Forty Eight Hour Return schedule charges a freight collection fee of 89.00, so regional_freight is the one that applies; retailer_van is excluded because the schedule does charge a freight collection fee, national_parcel because the schedule allows carrier pickup only and no label travels through the parcel network, and customer_delivered because the customer is not bringing a refrigerator to a store counter.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the confirmation of the collection slot so that it can be handed to the customer, who is the only one who may make it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Agreeing the day the crew comes to her home is the customer's own act; the unlock changes nothing on the records and is made once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Have the customer confirm the collection for the morning six days from the day of the call, which raises the confirmed collection request against the return.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The notice the collection is booked at is the value the collection slot notice policy computes, and the confirmation is the customer's own disposition of when a crew may come into her home.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_authorization_id: The return authorisation the collection belongs to, the same authorisation the booking was just recorded against. Basis: the tool docstring says of this argument 'the reference number of the return authorisation the collection belongs to, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one return authorisation.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.pickup_notice_days: 6 days. The schedule's collection lead days are 2. The appliance was delivered on White Glove Delivery and Installation, whose earliest slot is 5 days out, which is no slot inside the freight crew lead days of 5, so the crew notice is the freight crew notice days, 8. That service makes the water, waste and gas connections and takes the old item away, so the plumbed site days of 2 are added, giving 10. The membership stands active on Circle Total Annual, whose published return window extension of 45 days is at least the top member extension days, with nothing outstanding on its dues, so the top member priority days of 2 are taken off, leaving 8. The schedule charges a freight collection fee of 89.00 and the return has been standing since it was asked for on 2026-03-05, that is 12 days, longer than the schedule's 2 collection lead days, so the notice is counted in days the depot is open, five in every seven, and rounded up: 8 times 7 divided by 5 is 11.2, rounded up to 12. The return has been standing authorised since 2026-03-06, that is 11 days, longer than twice the schedule's 2 collection lead days, and two collection bookings now stand on it, so the notice is halved and rounded down: 12 halved is 6. The booking now standing was recorded on the day of the call, so no days have passed against the notice, and 6 is above the floor of 1. Any agent reading the same rows converges on 6.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.pickup_window: morning. Basis: the collection slot notice rule states 'The part of the day recorded on the collection is the one the customer agrees to when the slot is put to them, and no part of the day is recorded that the customer has not agreed to', and the customer says in the call that she confirms the slot 'choosing a morning' and that mornings are the only time she is reliably at home. Uniqueness: afternoon and all_day are excluded because she has said she is only reliably at home in the mornings, and business_hours is excluded because the collection is from a household address on a consumer profile, not business premises.

factor_trace: collection_route_window (parameter): the purchase order for serial RFX2843SS0417792 stands on White Glove Delivery and Installation, whose earliest slot is 5 days out, so the delivering service offers no slot inside the crew lead threshold of 3 days, and the Major Appliance Forty Eight Hour Return schedule charges a freight collection fee of 89.00; the first tier applies and the route window is the schedule's 7 label validity days plus the 7 freight slot days, that is 14. Baseline: the schedule's label validity days alone, 7.

reissued_booking_window (parameter): the return's history carries exactly one collection booking, recorded 2026-03-06 with a last usable day of 2026-03-13, which has passed, so the second tier applies and the first reissue reduction days of 3 are taken off. Baseline: nothing taken off, 0.

aged_authorisation_window (method): the return has stood authorised since 2026-03-06, that is 11 days, longer than the schedule's 7 label validity days but not longer than twice them, so the second tier applies and a quarter is taken off the 11 days left after the reduction and the result rounded down to a whole day, giving 8. Baseline method: the window left after the reduction is taken as counted, 11.

member_booking_hold (parameter): the membership stands active on Circle Total Annual, whose published return window extension is 45 days, at least the top member extension days, and its dues carry nothing outstanding, so the first tier applies and the top member hold days of 4 are added. Baseline: nothing added, 0.
schedule_open_days (no factor): a plain read of the schedule's label validity days, 7.
freight_collection_charge (no factor): a plain read of the schedule's freight collection fee, 89.00, which the route ladder tests.
window_after_reissue (no factor): plumbing, 14 less 3 and never below nothing, giving 11.
result (no factor): the measured window of 8 plus the membership hold of 4, held at or above the floor of 2, giving 12.

edges.condition: The return's history carries a collection booking entry naming the carrier that is to move the item whose last usable day is still to come, and the notice runs from the day that entry was recorded.
edges.policy_source: The earliest day the collection may be booked for is settled only after a collection booking naming the carrier that is to move the item stands recorded against the return with a last usable day that has not passed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only collection booking standing on the return when the call opens was recorded on 2026-03-06 with 2026-03-13 as its last usable day, four days before the day of the call, so no collection booking with a last usable day still to come stands against the return and the day the notice would run from is a booking that has lapsed.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Recording the fresh booking puts a collection booking dated 2026-03-17 with a last usable day of 2026-03-29 on the return, so the binding that reads the day the booking now standing was recorded takes 2026-03-17, nothing has yet passed against the notice, and two collection bookings stand on the return.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain of two problems with one edge, so there is only one order in which the writes can be made: the collection booking is recorded first and the slot is confirmed second. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying the call without the collection booking leaves the lapsed booking of 2026-03-06 as the only one standing: the count of bookings falls to one, so the waiting priority takes a quarter off rather than halving, giving 9 rather than 6, and eleven days have already passed since that booking was recorded, so the notice falls to the floor. The scored notice moves from 6 days to 1 day, and the confirmed collection day moves from 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-18.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The customer says only that the fridge is still in her hallway, that nobody has come for it and that she would like it collected, and later that she is only reliably at home in the mornings. She never mentions a collection booking, a carrier, a tracking reference, a last usable day or anything having lapsed, and she never suggests that something has to be sorted out first; when she is told a carrier has been arranged she reacts to what the agent has said and nothing more. If the agent never records a booking she neither reminds nor presses; she still confirms whatever slot is put to her.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_collection_slot_e0893723 reads the return authorisation only to copy the customer reference onto the new collection request; it never looks for a collection booking entry, never compares a last usable day with the day of the call, and raises no error when none stands. Called with no booking on the return it still writes the collection request faithfully, and the consequence shows up only in the notice the agent worked out being wrong against the terminal hash. issue_collection_booking_70222685 likewise checks nothing about the state of the return before writing its entry.
